# Wild Lake Studio | Talent Architecture and Artist Development

> Wild Lake Studio, known as Wild-Lake, is an independent talent architecture and artist development studio for creators across music, art, writing and film. Based across New York, Tampa, and Santiago; working worldwide.

Wild-Lake is point zero for starmaking.

Wild-Lake is an independent studio for artists, labels, galleries and agencies. We give critical direction, fix the structure behind the work, and build the systems that carry a career. We never take ownership or a percentage.

## Practice and engagement

[Talent Architecture — The Method](https://wildlakestudio.com/method/#method-talent-architecture)

Your practice is the asset. We find where it is breaking.

Talent Architecture is a capacity and boundary audit for creators whose workload has outgrown them. We dismantle the habits that drain you, build an operating framework that protects your autonomy, and step back. You keep your IP, your income, and your decisions.

The core offering is undivided attention. Close study of the artist, the work, and the conditions shaping both. We observe, listen, and stay with the material long enough to offer a precise response.

We scout talent and work with artists directly, or partner with record labels, galleries, and booking agencies. In either case, the artist enters the engagement willingly, on their own initiative or through a representative.

Artist Development works with the creator behind the work. Creative Development works with raw material across mediums and stages. Audience development, critical writing, and channels of encounter are creative infrastructure.

The Stewardship Subscription reserves availability between client-triggered interventions. Focused observation and editing alternate with periods of independent execution. Scope, response times, and reserved capacity are agreed in advance. Fixed project commissions and focused advisory engagements are also available.

Artists retain ownership and creative control. The studio takes no percentage of artist earnings. The studio retains its proprietary frameworks and licenses delivered framework materials for the client’s practice; public-facing writing transfers to the client upon final settlement. Refer to the Terms of Practice for the full agreement boundaries.

## Founder: the medium

Argelys Samuel Oriach is the founder and artistic director of Wild Lake Studio.

https://wildlakestudio.com/about-founder/

Argelys Samuel Oriach is a Dominican-born systems architect, performance artist, and artistic director based in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. He constructs systems and inhabits them. Performance governs his practice, and writing, voice, movement, design, and corporate roles are its forms.

He operates two laboratories: Seven Eighty Three (Lab 783), an independent systems design practice, and Wild Lake Studio, its research laboratory, which guides developing and independent artists. The studio operates from New York, Tampa, and Santiago, and works worldwide.

Wild Lake Studio formalizes Argelys's fifteen-year independent practice. It began in his freshman year at Wesleyan University, when he was initiated into the Eclectic Society and started producing live shows, organizing cultural space, and working alongside artists. Over those fifteen years he has guided twelve or more developing and independent multidisciplinary artists, providing structural stewardship, physical carrying capacity, and live production architecture.

Argelys builds infrastructure for artists on the same principles he applies to technical architecture: nothing decorative, and everything carries weight.

He was born in the Dominican Republic to a mother who is a housekeeper and writer and a father who is a facility maintainer and musician. His structural impulse surfaced at eleven, when he taught himself 3D design software to draft his parents' dream home. An architect later used that file for construction. After the 2008 financial crash, he applied to Phillips Academy Andover to design the conditions of his own life on purpose.

A method actor trained in the Alexander Technique, he spent the next sixteen years treating his body, voice, and daily life as a single structural instrument. In 2010 he attended Northwestern University's National High School Institute (Cherubs) theatre program and played Nick in a stage adaptation of The Handmaid's Tale. From there he studied somatic weight, posture, and human attention by inhabiting roles across institutions, physical staging, and corporate infrastructure.

That foundation fueled a twelve-year trajectory building organic growth systems. He served as Cynthia Nixon's social media manager for her 2018 campaign for governor of New York, then moved to architecting sovereign digital frameworks from first principles. He went on to build brand infrastructure at VinePair, direct brand marketing at Kickstarter, and lead organic growth at CookUnity. He approached these corporate roles as an undercover durational performance: a calculated effort to build his life out of poverty while auditing how complex systems scale from the inside out. That cycle recently closed with an intentional return to his body, breath, and voice.

Wild-Lake's method grew through the lived practice described here. The manual sets out how critique, structural honesty, artist wellbeing, and focused interventions operate within an engagement.

Performance governs how he works across writing, voice, movement, visual art, design, and acting for stage and screen. “Multidisciplinary” describes the range of media. “Performance artist” describes how he inhabits them.

At Wesleyan he sang with Ebony Singers, studying African-American religious music through performance, including traditional and contemporary gospel, spirituals, and hymns. He also took African drumming courses.

As a writer, he applies the same somatic and structural rigor to narrative in a maximalist, automatic, lyrical, stream-of-consciousness style. His focus remains the physical and digital mechanics beneath every medium.
- This Is Not a Love Story (Yankees): a digital short, published at thisisnotalovestory.net. It is a screenplay written in prose form.
- Graduation: a debut autofiction novel (in progress).
- Untitled One-Act Play (in progress).
- Untitled Pilot (in progress).

He majored in English at Wesleyan University, where he took extensive coursework in studio art and critical theory. His senior thesis was Breaking the circle of the plantation: Violence, affect and the ephemeral in Junot Díaz's Afro-Caribbean literary imagination.

The thesis positions The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao as an alternative archive of the diaspora. It examines Díaz's Afro-Caribbean literary imagination through queer theory, performance studies, affect studies, and critical race theory.

Argelys understands his approach through the architect and shaman archetypes. The architect gives the practice structure. The shaman attends to meaning, transition, and the artist's relationship to their work. Together they make him an alchemist, transforming raw material and lived experience into artistic form. These archetypes inform how he shapes the conditions around an artist while staying close to what the work means to them.

He reflects on his approach through four terms.

Investigation Understanding the foundations before proposing a structure. Asking what is present, what matters, and what the work needs.

Experimentation Learning through making and lived experience. Letting what happens in practice inform the next decision.

Emotional clarity Allowing time to understand a response rather than treating urgency as direction.

Invitation Entering a creative relationship by mutual recognition and consent. Guidance is offered within a relationship the artist chooses.

## The Method: the manual

https://wildlakestudio.com/method/

### The Method: Diagnosis & Scope

https://wildlakestudio.com/method/#method-overview

The manual The Method: Diagnosis & Scope Traditional A&R and institutional pipelines can extract creative output faster than an artist's internal and operational infrastructure can carry it. Delivery demands then exceed the capacity required to sustain the work. Wild-Lake is the structural counterpart. We build the conditions, capacity, and artistic rigor required for work that endures. An engagement may be initiated by the artist or commissioned by a manager, label, gallery, or agency. The artist enters willingly and retains control of the work. The practice begins with the assets the artist already holds: raw material, rights, skills, audience relationships, and working infrastructure. We identify what those assets can support, agree an intervention, observe it in use, and revise it against the result. Wild-Lake takes 0% IP ownership and 0% revenue share. Meet the founder

### Terms of the Practice

https://wildlakestudio.com/method/#method-terms

Terms of the Practice Structural Design Organizing time, space, resources, habits, and boundaries so the work can be made and sustained. Talent Architecture Fortifying the person carrying the work: their judgment, capacity, autonomy, and relationships, within those working conditions. Sovereign A&R Developing raw material through close study, critique, direction, and critical framing. The conditions support the creator, and the creator develops the material. The artist retains 100% ownership and creative control.

### The Mechanics of Talent Architecture

https://wildlakestudio.com/method/#method-mechanics

The Mechanics of Talent Architecture Talent Architecture treats a career as an interdependent system of creative assets, working conditions, capacity, and commitments. The four orbital principles below define what we examine and how the artist builds durable career equity. 1. Core Mass Condense the raw material before exposing it to market pressure. We protect studio time, research, rehearsal, and revision so the work develops density and artistic rigor. Market exposure follows material the artist can stand behind and infrastructure that can carry the response. 2. Orbital Velocity Calibrate output to the artist's actual capacity. We examine the release schedule, workload, income requirements, and recovery time, then set working rhythms, access boundaries, and decision responsibilities. Capacity and delivery are reviewed together so output does not consume the person sustaining it. 3. Elliptical Cycles Use both public and quiet phases intentionally. Perihelion describes periods of release, exhibition, production, and live performance. Aphelion describes research, rest, and raw gestation. We scope commitments and resources for each phase so quiet development contributes to the next body of work rather than being treated as failure. 4. Escape Velocity Build enough independent capacity to leave predatory deals, reactive trends, and draining environments. Retained rights, direct audience relationships, and working infrastructure generate leverage without surrendering equity. Wild-Lake takes 0% IP ownership and 0% revenue share, so the artist retains the assets and decisions required to change course.

### Execution: Demolition, Critique, Honesty, Cadence

https://wildlakestudio.com/method/#method-practice

Execution: Demolition, Critique, Honesty, Cadence Controlled Demolition Audit the practice with the artist. Identify the brittle systems, inherited commitments, and habits that exceed available capacity. Agree what to remove, retain, or rebuild, then establish working conditions that protect the artist's autonomy. Test the changes in actual work before treating them as settled. Critique & Revision Study raw material closely across visual art, sculpture, installation, writing, music, film, and performance. Offer direct interpretations and revisions that the artist can test, use, or reject. Examine ego loops and dependence on external validation when they drain stamina or distort decisions. Evaluate changes through the work itself. Conversational Brutalism Expose the load-bearing limits without euphemism: what the practice can carry, what it costs to deliver, and where commitments exceed available time, resources, or physical capacity. Make those conditions explicit so the artist can decide what changes and what support is required. Observation & Absence Alternate high-density interventions with total absence from day-to-day execution. We observe, critique, and agree the intervention, then step back so the artist works without surveillance. At the next agreed review, artist and studio examine what happened and refine the intervention through use.

### Institutional Alignment: Managers, Agents, Labels & Curators

https://wildlakestudio.com/method/#method-stakeholders

Institutional Alignment: Managers, Agents, Labels & Curators Wild-Lake works with managers, booking agents, labels, galleries, curators, and A&R executives as a defensive buffer and developmental engine around the artist. We do not replace those roles. We examine how institutional demands affect the capacity, artistic rigor, and long-term value of the underlying creative asset. Before work begins, the artist, representative, and studio agree the scope, decision responsibilities, delivery timeline, access boundaries, and review points. The artist confirms participation and determines what material or information may be shared. A third-party commission creates no claim on the artist's work. When demands exceed capacity, we make the conflict explicit and revise the scope, resources, or timeline with the parties involved. Delivery is planned against actual conditions. Each review checks whether those boundaries hold, whether the intervention supports the work, and what must change to prevent over-extraction.

### Artist Wellbeing & Development Protocols

https://wildlakestudio.com/method/#method-wellbeing

Artist Wellbeing & Development Protocols The pace, boundaries, and expectations of an engagement account for the artist's history, physical experience, and present capacity. The artist decides what to share and can pause, decline, or change direction at any time. We support artists rebuilding self-trust after narcissistic abuse, examining narcissistic patterns within themselves, or both. The work examines harmful relational patterns and establishes boundaries that protect creative autonomy. Trauma-informed pacing leaves room for care beyond the studio. During a retained engagement, Argelys may guide somatic, creative, or operational practices selected with the artist. Touch and co-regulation are optional and require explicit, ongoing consent. Participation in a practice is never a condition of retaining ownership or creative control. Explore the practices Development Protocols Active listening, structural honesty, automatic writing, grounding, movement, and vision quests, alongside operational systems for inquiries, communication, payments, and direct publishing. Each practice is optional. The artist can pause, decline, or change direction. Explore the protocols →

### Ownership, Universe API & Governance

https://wildlakestudio.com/method/#method-sovereignty

Ownership, Universe API & Governance The artist retains 100% of their IP and creative control. Wild-Lake takes 0% IP ownership and 0% revenue share. Asset-based leverage remains with the artist, including rights, income, and direct audience relationships. An upfront monthly Stewardship Subscription reserves agreed capacity for client-triggered interventions. Scope, response windows, access limits, and review points are set before the engagement begins. Fixed commissions and focused advisory scopes are available when the work has a defined boundary. Universe API is Argelys's macro-micro diagnostic framework. It connects the conditions of the wider system with the artist's day-to-day capacity and decisions. It governs how interventions are scoped, tested in real conditions, and revised through use. Each intervention follows a closed loop: identify the constraint and the assets available, agree the change and the evidence to review, deploy it, observe its effect on the practice, and refine it with the artist. The review governs the next intervention and keeps the agreed scope proportional to the work. Engagement formats and fees · Terms of Practice · Begin an engagement

## Past and current clients

The roster includes past and current engagements and does not imply every engagement is active. Profiles describe each practice from Wild-Lake’s perspective. Interpretation is the studio’s reading, not necessarily the artist’s stated intention. Locations belong in full biographies and profile details, not in introductory role lists.

- [Aissa Rose Gueye](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#aissa-gueye): Senegalese-American writer-director, creative director, actress, and model. Her practice spans film, photography, writing, and performance. Lives and works: New York / Los Angeles.
- [Argelys Samuel Oriach](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#argelys-oriach): Dominican-born visual, performance, and movement artist, artistic director, actor, writer, vocalist, songwriter, and the author of This Is Not a Love Story . Currently writing a pilot, a play, and his debut autofiction novel, Graduation . Lives and works: New York. Born in the Dominican Republic, Argelys Samuel Oriach was raised by a housekeeper and a facility maintainer, and learned in adulthood that his mother was a writer and his father a musician, though neither pursued their craft. Because of this, he understands creative capacity entirely through the physical infrastructure required to sustain it. A method actor trained in the Alexander Technique, Oriach studies how people look, listen, move, and affect one another. This Is Not a Love Story is a screenplay written in prose form.
- [Drew Rutland](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#drew-rutland): Producer, fashion designer, and stylist working with high-profile talent and fashion brands. His background spans VIP and influencer relations, event production, and fashion design. Lives and works: New York.
- [Emily Wilson](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#emily-wilson): Food writer, photographer, and author of The Angel , an IACP Award-winning newsletter about food, restaurants, and the people who shape how we eat. Lives and works: New York.
- [Jessica Wilson](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#jessica-wilson): Multidisciplinary artist exploring how virtual systems register in bodies, objects, and everyday infrastructure. Lives and works: New York / Amsterdam.
- [Jimmy Andrew O’Keeffe](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#jimmy-andrew-okeeffe): Producer and filmmaker at North Six. His work includes projects for Nike and Frédéric Malle, and he produced The Sun Is In My Eyes (2024). Lives and works: New York.
- [Jordy Oriach](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#jordy-oriach): Left-handed power. An unconventional path from the Dominican Republic through junior college, New Mexico, and the University of Georgia. Built through persistence and progression. Lives and works: New York.
- [Kyle Roach](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#kyle-roach): Actor for stage and screen and model with a background in music production at Capitol Records. Lives and works: New York.
- [Patrick Schlotterback](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#patrick-schlotterback): Patrick Schlotterback is an artist working in fibers and ceramics. His work gives feeling and emotion physical form through a distinct material language. Lives and works: New York.
- [Sophia Jennings](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#sophia-jennings): Writer and filmmaker. Director of Story at MakeMake, working across film, editorial, and advertising. Lives and works: Los Angeles.
- [Timo Sassen](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#timo-sassen): Antwerp-born fashion designer working in swimwear and now developing a full collection. His practice brings hands-on construction to clothing made for bodily expression. Lives and works: New York.
- [Zachary Reed Kantor](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#zachary-reed-kantor): Design director and musician. Working across product, branding, graphic, and motion design, he leads design at GIPHY. Lives and works: New York.

Emily Wilson is also a photographer; she studied photography alongside a double major in English and Sociology at Wesleyan. Sophia Jennings co-wrote and co-directed Sparks (2025) with Jake Davies; film information: https://www.instagram.com/sparks_thefilm/. Jimmy Andrew O’Keeffe produced The Sun Is In My Eyes (2024), directed and co-produced by Pablo Tapia Pla. ## Quiet Creek magazine and tools

Quiet Creek is Wild-Lake’s magazine, not a separate agency. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/quietcreekmag/. Its first essay, The Infrastructure Has an Inner Life, was published November 4, 2026 as the studio’s reading of Jessica Wilson’s work. Fountain (Weeping Outlet), 2024 is the cover; The Commute, 2025 and Siren, 2026 appear inline. Images supplied by diez gallery. The essay discusses infrastructure, attention, capitalism, whiteness, and the living world; those interpretations should not be presented as the artist’s declared themes.

Legacy /blog/ URLs redirect to /magazine/. Architectural Mirror is a simple one-to-four-card browser tool with notes and export. Quiet Creek Tarot is the separate installable, offline-capable app at https://mirror.wildlakestudio.com/app/. Readings stay on the device; no account or sign-in is required. These tools are distinct from the magazine.

## Responsibility and governance

Wild-Lake states that a fraction of every studio retainer supports freshwater defense, lake protection, and public land conservation. No percentage or recipient organization is specified. Terms of Practice cover retainers and fixed project fees, client IP, studio framework licensing, confidentiality, environmental allocation, and New York jurisdiction.

The website uses self-hosted fonts, styles, scripts, and native browser interactions. No Spotify embed, remote font request, or third-party analytics script is shipped. External services are reached through ordinary links. Hosting is provided by Cloudflare. The contact form prepares a draft in the visitor’s email app; it does not submit to a studio database.

Seven Eighty Three and Universe API are distinct from Wild-Lake; Universe API is a systems design framework, not a callable web API.

## Engagements & Pricing

https://wildlakestudio.com/pricing/

Engagements protect the artist and sustain the practice. Wild-Lake works on a cross-subsidy model. Established artists fund capacity for rising artists, and that funding creates no claim on the work of the artist it supports. Every artist retains ownership and creative control.

Established artists: retainer availability for text and voice notes, agreed response windows, limited urgent calls, and occasional deep intensives. Management and creative approval sit outside the engagement. Retainer and intensive fees are agreed individually.

Rising artists: a subsidized Stewardship Subscription for higher-frequency ongoing development and operational infrastructure. Eligibility rests on practice and need; inability to pay is one factor. Scope, expectations, and participation are agreed together. A sliding scale follows need and available capacity, with the rate agreed individually.

Fixed project fee: Creative Infrastructure commissions and defined editorial work. Scope and fee are agreed before work begins.

Access is async-first within clear boundaries. Artists may pause, decline, or change direction. Touch and co-regulation require explicit ongoing consent. Artists retain ownership, creative control, and direct audience relationships. Wild-Lake takes no percentage of masters, publishing, or touring. No public fee amounts are listed. Begin by sharing the work, determining fit, rhythm, and scope, then agreeing retainer, subscription, or fixed-fee terms.

## Name & Number

https://wildlakestudio.com/numerology/

Wild-Lake’s browser-only numerology tool calculates Expression, Soul Urge, and Personality from a birth name; Life Path and Birthday from a birth date; and Maturity when both are supplied. It uses Pythagorean letter values, lets the user count Y as a vowel or consonant, retains master numbers 11, 22, and 33 at each reduction, and shows the arithmetic. Life Path reduces month, day, and year separately before combining. Original reflection prompts focus on creative capacity, desire, boundaries, and agency. Numbers are symbolic prompts, not verdicts. Inputs are never saved or sent; a reading and optional notes can be downloaded as a local text file.

## Homepage: practice and offerings

### Our focus

The artist: Artist Development. Support for the person behind the work and the capacity to keep making. The practice: Existential Mechanics. Aligning the life an artist leads with the work they want to build. The venture: Sovereign A&R. Sustained attention to raw material, in any form and at any stage. The structure: Creative Infrastructure. We help the world catch up to the artist, building lasting ways to encounter the work.

### How we work

Nature is brutalist. Nothing in it is decorative, and everything carries weight. We build infrastructure for artists under that same principle. We work closely with the artist, then give them space to execute. The Method sets out our approach to critique, structural honesty, and the rhythm of an engagement.

### Development Protocols

Explore the practices Argelys may guide during a retained engagement, including active listening, automatic writing, movement, and vision quests. The selection follows the artist and the work.

### Ways to work together

The core offering is undivided attention. Close study of the artist, the work, and the conditions shaping both. Sovereign A&R: Focused creative attention to raw material, artistic direction, and the context through which work reaches an audience. Talent Architecture: Structural support for the person sustaining the practice, with boundaries and working conditions that make independence possible. Creative Infrastructure: Fixed-scope commissions that build the foundations of a practice: audience assets, platform setup, and live production architecture.

### Your work stays yours.

The artist retains ownership and creative control. We work on an agreed Stewardship Subscription or fixed project fee.

### Let’s begin.

Tell us about your work, or the artists you work with, and what support is needed.

## Laboratory relationship

He operates two laboratories: Seven Eighty Three (Lab 783), an independent systems design practice, and Wild Lake Studio, its research laboratory, which guides developing and independent artists.
